basis: Full statements and constraints were checked against the official Codeforces editorials or official LeetCode problem pages. Generated labels that described surface wording rather than the actual solution were removed; retained patterns use the canonical taxonomy.

problems.solution: Sort interval endpoints and sweep them with two pointers, counting earlier starts that are not strictly beyond the current end.
Express the change caused by moving the first element of a chosen subarray to its end, then maximize the resulting alternating gain with prefix differences and Kadane-style scans.
Order numbers by their high-to-low bit vectors, equivalently descending numeric order, so each successive bit obtains the longest possible all-set prefix.
Convert every required MEX value into a forbidden integer interval and use a difference array to output exactly the integers covered by no forbidden interval.
Build required and forbidden integer intervals, sort the required intervals, and count valid subsets with a two-pointer dynamic program over eligible values.
Reverse the deletions, maintaining active champion breakpoints in an ordered set and interval sums in a Fenwick tree.
A valid value set must be the union of two opposing arithmetic progressions; test the two possible gaps and multiply the independent arrangement factorials.
Mark target-functional-graph paths needed by mismatched vertices, reject incompatible terminal components, then simulate increments and pointer moves along a valid path.
Count bracket-pair decompositions with Catalan-derived factors and a convolution-style DP, then use binomial inversion to obtain exact common-pair counts.
Maintain matrix rank and inverse information with Gaussian elimination, using perfect matchings and small-rank updates to construct the minimum number of removals.
The winner depends only on whether ones are at least as numerous as zeroes, so count the two values.
Derive the feasible first-row and first-column overlap from k, place those small values, and fill all remaining matrix cells arbitrarily.
Collect every misplaced position and check with two pointers whether reversing exactly those selected values sorts the permutation.
After telescoping the score, fix its last element and maintain the m-1 smallest earlier values in a max-heap.
Sort ratings, count how many increasing-parent trees contain each possible edge, and sum every edge's weighted contribution using suffix sums.
Map divisible binary substrings to equal alternating-prefix residues modulo three, balance the residue frequencies, and construct a string with three ones.
Precompute the best equalized value for every minimum-maximum pair with a radical sieve and interval DP, then count subsequences by their endpoints.
Generate radical-divisibility blockers, compress each DP row into a few breakpoints, and sum endpoint contributions over ranges with prefix sums.
Synthesize a compact legal expression for derangement counts, using DP-built constants, threshold expressions, factorial products, and the derangement recurrence or formula.
